primary_frame: Identify which employee attributes, if any, are predictive of performance rating
alternative_frames: Segment employees by salary band and test whether bands differ on performance or satisfaction
Model satisfaction score as a function of work-environment features (remote_pct, commute_minutes, team_size)
Detect clusters of employee profiles and characterise each cluster
required_checks: Test pairwise correlations between all numeric features and performance_rating before modelling
Check distribution of performance_rating for normality and outliers
Verify salary_band is not a proxy for an ordinal variable by inspecting level frequencies and feature distributions per band
Run a baseline permutation or shuffle test to confirm any observed signal exceeds chance
Assess multicollinearity among predictor features before interpreting regression coefficients
framing_risks: No explicit target variable is declared in the profile; performance_rating is assumed as the target based on column semantics
With 800 rows and 9 candidate predictors, spurious correlations are plausible at conventional significance thresholds
Salary band level frequencies and sample rows show no obvious ordinal relationship with experience or performance, suggesting bands may be arbitrarily assigned
Zero nulls across all columns is unusual for real HR data and may indicate synthetic or pre-cleaned data, limiting generalisability conclusions
Commute_minutes distribution is right-skewed (median 16, max 120); outlier-sensitive methods may overfit the tail
